title: Roast pork steaks with peppers and green beans

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything is whole food or a plain cupboard staple: pork, vegetables, olive oil, spices and lemon.

supermarket.reason: Pork shoulder steaks, new potatoes, peppers, green beans and fennel seeds are all everyday supermarket buys.

basic_kitchen.reason: Only one roasting tray is needed, and crushing fennel seeds is easy with a knife or rolling pin.

works.reason: At 220°C, the 20 minute head start on the potatoes and 27 minutes for the shoulder steaks should give tender veg and cooked-through pork, with the beans blistered in the last 12 minutes, enough for four.

honest_times.reason: Twenty minutes is realistic for halving potatoes, cutting onions and peppers, trimming beans and seasoning the pork, and 20+15+12 matches the 47 minute cook time.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning, including the lemon, appears in the steps, and nothing unlisted is used.

seasonal_feel.reason: A tray roast of new potatoes, peppers and 300g of green beans suits early July, and the beans are a real portion of the dish rather than a garnish, though the pork and peppers lead the title.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, plain British English that a beginner can follow.

hearty_healthy.reason: Pork, potatoes and plenty of vegetables make a balanced family dinner.
